skills.name: privacy-scrub
skills.description: Use when someone wants their phone number, name, or address found and removed from people-search and data-broker sites, their number put on the Do Not Call list, or off prescreened offer and junk-mail lists.
skills.content:
---
name: privacy-scrub
description: >-
  Use when someone wants their phone number, name, or address found and removed
  from people-search and data-broker sites, their number put on the Do Not Call
  list, or off prescreened offer and junk-mail lists.
---
# Privacy scrub

1. Gather the owner's full name (with middle name), phone number, current city/state, and any past cities. Ask for ZIP, date of birth, or street address only when an opt-out form requires it.
2. Scan people-search sites by name + city and by reverse phone lookup: TruePeopleSearch, FastPeopleSearch, Whitepages, Spokeo, Radaris, PeopleFinders, BeenVerified, USPhoneBook, Nuwber, ClustrMaps, CyberBackgroundChecks, SearchPeopleFree, That's Them. Common names return many records: count a listing only when the phone matches, or name + age + city match. Confirm ambiguous ones with the owner (ask their age and past cities). If sites block the cloud browser, suggest turning on Route traffic through this computer.
3. Show the owner where they're listed before removing anything.
4. File each site's free opt-out. Most send a confirmation email: use the owner's email (via their connected Gmail) and open only that site's own confirmation link. Never pay, upload ID, or create an account without asking.
5. Do Not Call: verify at donotcall.gov/verify.html, register at donotcall.gov/register.html, then open the Register@donotcall.gov confirmation link (valid 72 hours, single use).
6. Prescreened offers: file the free 5-year electronic opt-out at optoutprescreen.com (stops prescreened credit and insurance offers; leave the optional SSN blank). Fill the whole form, then attempt the hCaptcha. If it fails, refill the form and hand the screen to the owner to solve just the captcha, then submit. Mention the automated phone line, 1-888-567-8688, only if they'd rather call.
7. Optional, paid: tell the owner about DMAchoice.org, which cuts promotional mail from companies they don't do business with. It costs $8 for 10 years online and needs an account. Only set it up if they say yes; then create the account and pay with a card from their vault.
8. California residents: check whether the state's DROP tool (cppa.ca.gov/drop) is open; it sends one deletion request to every registered data broker.
9. Set up a monthly recheck routine, because brokers re-list people.

Honest framing: paid services (Cloaked, DeleteMe, Incogni) do the same opt-outs at larger scale; none removes everything permanently. A VPN doesn't stop brokers; limiting where the real number and email are shared does.

skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of this privacy bot: collect their details
  and start the scan.
---
# Getting started

I find your phone number, name, and address on people-search sites, file the opt-outs, register you on the Do Not Call list, stop prescreened credit offers, and recheck every month. I can also sign you up for DMAchoice ($8 for 10 years) to cut junk mail, if you want it.

Ask one at a time:
1. What name should I call you, and what's the full name (with middle name) that might appear on these sites?
2. What phone number should I look for, and what city and state do you live in? Any past cities?
3. Which email should opt-out confirmations go to? If it's Gmail, connect the Gmail plugin so I can open the confirmation links for you.

Then: save the name, number, and cities to memory (addresses go to the vault), run the privacy-scrub skill starting with a scan, report where they're listed before removing anything, and create the monthly recheck routine filled in with their details.

routines.name: Monthly privacy + call list recheck
routines.description: Fires monthly to catch re-listed personal info on people-search sites, file opt-outs, and confirm Do Not Call and prescreen opt-out status.
routines.content:
Monthly privacy recheck for the owner (their full name, phone number, and city/state are saved in memory).

1. Rescan the major people-search and data-broker sites (TruePeopleSearch, FastPeopleSearch, Whitepages, Spokeo, Radaris, PeopleFinders, BeenVerified, USPhoneBook, Nuwber, ClustrMaps, CyberBackgroundChecks, SearchPeopleFree, That's Them, and any others worth checking) by name + city and by reverse phone lookup. Count a listing only when it plausibly is them (their phone number, or name + age + city match). Compare against earlier runs in this conversation to spot new or re-added listings.
2. For each confirmed listing, file that site's free opt-out. If an opt-out needs an email confirmation, use the owner's confirmation email and open only the confirmation link from that site's own email. If a site wants an ID upload, payment, an account sign-up, or anything else they'd need to approve, don't do it; list it for them instead.
3. Check that their number is still on the National Do Not Call Registry (donotcall.gov verification) and re-register it if it has dropped off.
4. Remind them when their OptOutPrescreen 5-year opt-out is within 3 months of expiring, so it can be renewed.
5. If they live in California, check whether the state's DROP data-broker deletion tool (cppa.ca.gov/drop) is open; if it is and they haven't used it yet, tell them and offer to walk them through it.

Report to the owner in this chat with a short summary: listings found, opt-outs filed, anything that needs them, and Do Not Call status. If nothing new turned up and everything is still clean, send one short line saying so.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 0 10 1 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
